note: The integration suite was not idempotent against a database another run already used. That was the finding, and this file was its reproduction: the tests and passes that fail when the suite runs against the database the first run left behind. It is a record, not a permission. tools/verify-suite-idempotency.php fails on any test outside its pass-aware entry, fails when a listed test stops needing the exemption in a recorded pass, and fails when an entry passes its expiry, so the list can only ever shrink. The six recorded tests each executed the removal their entry named, and the process-scoped fixture lifecycle now withdraws every newly published run-unique integration definition together with its live schema installation after each suite run while retaining the explicitly shared replay fixtures. The record is therefore empty for both the repeated and reverse-class-order passes, and anything that fails now is new.

scope.note: `repeat` runs the integration suite again against the database the first full run left behind. `reverse` then lists the same integration classes in reverse while preserving declaration order inside each class. Appended to the initial full-suite execution, these are three consecutive runs against one database. Each PHPUnit process snapshots the migrated definition catalog and atomically withholds the installation and rejects the current version of every run-unique definition it added before it exits, while an explicit bounded set of stable replay fixtures remains available for the next pass. Transient fixture contracts therefore do not consume the next run's live OpenAPI definition allowance.
scope.engines_note: Two fields carry two different claims, and conflating them would make the gate lie in one direction or the other. `observed_on` is fact: the engines on which this exact failure was seen. `applies_to` is scope: the engines on which the entry excuses a failure. `passes` limits both claims to the execution passes that actually produced the record. A test failing on an engine or pass outside that scope is a new violation; an entry whose test passes on an observed engine in a recorded pass is stale and must be deleted. An engine in `applies_to` but not in `observed_on` is therefore neither excused into silence nor asserted as fact. CI now executes both enforced passes on MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.
